FICTIONAL TEST DOCUMENT. In the matter of Arun Traders versus Meena Exports. The appellant issued a cheque for rupees four lakh towards repayment of a trade debt. The cheque was returned unpaid by the bank with the remark funds insufficient. The respondent filed a complaint alleging an offence of dishonour of cheque under the statute. The trial court convicted the appellant and imposed a fine equal to twice the cheque amount. On appeal the central question was whether a written demand notice was served on the drawer within thirty days of receiving information of the return. The court held that service of the demand notice on the drawer is mandatory before any prosecution, and that a complaint filed without such notice is premature and cannot be entertained. The court further observed that the drawer must be given fifteen days after receipt of the notice to make payment. Since the record showed the notice was dispatched to an incorrect address and never delivered, the conviction was set aside. The appeal was allowed and the fine already deposited was ordered to be refunded to the appellant. The court added that nothing in this judgment prevents the respondent from pursuing a civil suit for recovery.
